stopp.criteria: Digoxin at dose >125mcg/day with impaired renal function
stopp.rationale: Risk of digoxin toxicity; reduced renal clearance in elderly

stopp.criteria: Loop diuretic as first-line treatment for hypertension
stopp.rationale: Safer, more effective antihypertensives available; risk of dehydration/electrolyte imbalance

stopp.criteria: Thiazide diuretic with history of gout
stopp.rationale: May exacerbate gout by increasing uric acid levels

stopp.criteria: Amiodarone as first-line antiarrhythmic in supraventricular tachyarrhythmias
stopp.rationale: Higher risk of side effects than beta-blockers, digoxin, verapamil, or diltiazem for rate control

stopp.criteria: Beta-blocker in combination with verapamil or diltiazem
stopp.rationale: Risk of heart block and severe bradycardia

stopp.criteria: Aldosterone antagonist with potassium-sparing agent without monitoring serum potassium
stopp.rationale: Risk of dangerous hyperkalaemia; requires regular potassium monitoring

stopp.criteria: ACE inhibitor or ARB with potassium-sparing diuretic without potassium monitoring
stopp.rationale: Risk of hyperkalaemia, particularly in older adults with reduced renal function

stopp.criteria: Non-selective beta-blocker with COPD or asthma
stopp.rationale: Risk of bronchospasm

stopp.criteria: Antimuscarinic bronchodilator with narrow-angle glaucoma
stopp.rationale: May exacerbate glaucoma

stopp.criteria: Aspirin with no history of cardiovascular disease (primary prevention in >70)
stopp.rationale: No evidence of benefit for primary prevention in elderly; bleeding risk outweighs

stopp.criteria: Aspirin plus clopidogrel for secondary stroke prevention without coronary stent
stopp.rationale: No evidence of added benefit over single agent; increased bleeding risk

stopp.criteria: Aspirin or clopidogrel with concurrent anticoagulant without clear indication
stopp.rationale: Significantly increased bleeding risk without added benefit in most cases

stopp.criteria: Tricyclic antidepressant with dementia, narrow-angle glaucoma, cardiac conduction abnormalities, prostatism, or prior urinary retention
stopp.rationale: Strong anticholinergic effects; risk of worsening cognitive impairment, urinary retention, glaucoma

stopp.criteria: Initiation of tricyclic antidepressant as first-line antidepressant treatment
stopp.rationale: Higher risk of adverse effects than SSRIs/SNRIs; not first-line in elderly

stopp.criteria: Neuroleptics/antipsychotics used as long-term hypnotics
stopp.rationale: Risk of confusion, falls, stroke; not indicated for insomnia in elderly

stopp.criteria: Benzodiazepine for ≥4 weeks
stopp.rationale: Risk of prolonged sedation, confusion, impaired balance, falls, road traffic accidents; short-term use (<4 weeks) only

stopp.criteria: Antipsychotics for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia unless non-pharmacological approaches have failed and symptoms are severe
stopp.rationale: Increased risk of cerebrovascular events and mortality in dementia patients

stopp.criteria: Opioids without concurrent laxative
stopp.rationale: Risk of severe constipation, impaction; nearly all opioid users need laxative prophylaxis

stopp.criteria: Opioids long-term for mild-moderate pain where paracetamol or NSAIDs would suffice
stopp.rationale: Risk of dependence, falls, confusion; WHO pain ladder should be followed

stopp.criteria: NSAID with eGFR <50 mL/min/1.73m²
stopp.rationale: Risk of further deterioration of renal function

stopp.criteria: Metformin with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m²
stopp.rationale: Risk of lactic acidosis with severe renal impairment

stopp.criteria: PPI for uncomplicated peptic ulcer disease or erosive oesophagitis at full therapeutic dose for >8 weeks
stopp.rationale: Dose reduction or earlier discontinuation indicated; long-term risk of C. difficile, osteoporosis, hypomagnesaemia

stopp.criteria: Drugs likely to cause constipation in patients with chronic constipation
stopp.rationale: Risk of worsening constipation and faecal impaction

stopp.criteria: NSAID with history of peptic ulcer or GI bleeding without concurrent PPI
stopp.rationale: Risk of peptic ulcer recurrence/GI bleeding

stopp.criteria: NSAID with concurrent anticoagulant
stopp.rationale: Significantly increased risk of GI bleeding

stopp.criteria: Long-term corticosteroids (>3 months) for conditions other than specified indications without osteoporosis prophylaxis
stopp.rationale: Risk of osteoporotic fractures; calcium/vitamin D and bisphosphonate should be co-prescribed

stopp.criteria: Antimuscarinic drugs with dementia or chronic cognitive impairment
stopp.rationale: Risk of worsening cognitive impairment and confusion

stopp.criteria: Alpha-1 selective alpha blocker in patients with symptomatic orthostatic hypotension or micturition syncope
stopp.rationale: Risk of syncope and falls

stopp.criteria: Sulfonylurea with long duration of action in type 2 diabetes
stopp.rationale: Risk of prolonged hypoglycaemia in elderly; shorter-acting agents preferred

stopp.criteria: Concurrent use of two or more opioids
stopp.rationale: Risk of opioid toxicity, respiratory depression; usually indicates need for specialist review

stopp.criteria: Concurrent opioid and benzodiazepine
stopp.rationale: Risk of severe respiratory depression and death; FDA boxed warning

stopp.criteria: Regular opioids without assessment of risk of falls
stopp.rationale: Opioids increase fall risk significantly in elderly; risk assessment required

stopp.criteria: Concurrent use of 2 or more drugs with anticholinergic properties
stopp.rationale: Risk of increased anticholinergic toxicity: confusion, constipation, urinary retention, dry mouth, tachycardia

stopp.criteria: Antimuscarinic drugs with closed-angle glaucoma
stopp.rationale: Risk of acute exacerbation of glaucoma

stopp.criteria: Antimuscarinic drugs with benign prostatic hyperplasia
stopp.rationale: Risk of acute urinary retention

stopp.criteria: Benzodiazepine in patients with history of falls in past 3 months
stopp.rationale: Sedative drugs are the most important reversible risk factor for falls in elderly

stopp.criteria: Neuroleptic/antipsychotic drugs in patients with history of falls
stopp.rationale: Increased risk of sedation, orthostatic hypotension, and further falls

stopp.criteria: Vasodilator drugs in patients with persistent postural hypotension
stopp.rationale: Risk of syncope and falls

stopp.criteria: Two concurrent drugs of same class (duplicate prescribing)
stopp.rationale: Optimize monotherapy before adding second agent of same class; increased side effect risk without proportional benefit

start.criteria: Statin therapy with documented history of coronary, cerebral or peripheral vascular disease
start.rationale: Proven secondary prevention benefit; reduces cardiovascular events and mortality

start.criteria: ACE inhibitor or ARB in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
start.rationale: Reduces mortality and hospitalisation in HFrEF; first-line guideline therapy

start.criteria: Beta-blocker in stable heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
start.rationale: Proven mortality reduction in HFrEF when stable; MERIT-HF, CIBIS-II evidence

start.criteria: Appropriate antithrombotic therapy in atrial fibrillation
start.rationale: Reduces risk of stroke; DOACs preferred over warfarin in most elderly patients

start.criteria: Antihypertensive therapy where systolic BP consistently >150mmHg
start.rationale: Reduces cardiovascular events even in very elderly (>80 years); HYVET trial evidence

start.criteria: Regular inhaled beta-2 agonist or antimuscarinic bronchodilator for mild to moderate asthma or COPD
start.rationale: Essential for symptom control and prevention of exacerbations

start.criteria: Regular inhaled corticosteroid for moderate-severe asthma or COPD with frequent exacerbations
start.rationale: Reduces exacerbation frequency and improves lung function

start.criteria: SSRI or SNRI for moderate-severe depressive symptoms
start.rationale: First-line pharmacotherapy for depression in elderly; SSRIs preferred over TCAs

start.criteria: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor for mild-moderate Alzheimer's dementia
start.rationale: Modest symptomatic benefit in mild-moderate Alzheimer's

start.criteria: Vitamin D and calcium supplement in patients with known osteoporosis or fragility fracture
start.rationale: Reduces risk of further fractures; should be combined with bisphosphonate in most cases

start.criteria: Bisphosphonate or denosumab in patients on long-term systemic corticosteroids
start.rationale: Prevents glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis

start.criteria: Vitamin D supplement in elderly patients who are housebound or experiencing falls or with osteopenia
start.rationale: Vitamin D deficiency common in elderly; supplementation reduces fall risk

start.criteria: PPI with concurrent NSAID prescription in patient with peptic ulcer history
start.rationale: Reduces risk of GI bleeding from NSAID use

start.criteria: Fibre supplement for chronic, symptomatic diverticular disease with constipation
start.rationale: Prevents exacerbations and complications

start.criteria: Metformin as first-line oral antidiabetic in type 2 diabetes
start.rationale: First-line therapy; proven cardiovascular benefit; cost-effective

start.criteria: ACE inhibitor or ARB in diabetes with evidence of nephropathy (proteinuria or microalbuminuria)
start.rationale: Slows progression of diabetic nephropathy; renoprotective

start.criteria: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) as first-line analgesic for mild pain
start.rationale: Safest first-line analgesic in elderly; WHO pain ladder step 1

start.criteria: Annual influenza vaccine
start.rationale: Reduces influenza-related hospitalization and mortality in elderly

start.criteria: Pneumococcal vaccine per guidelines
start.rationale: Reduces invasive pneumococcal disease risk in elderly

start.criteria: Anticoagulant in chronic atrial fibrillation
start.rationale: Stroke prevention; DOACs preferred over warfarin for most elderly patients due to lower bleeding risk
